chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abu Saeed al-Raqam, from Salih ibn Uqba, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat the pomegranate with its lining, for it tans (hardens/strengthens) the stomach and increases the intellect.'

key_terms.بِشَحْمِهِ: With its lining/fat (referring to the inner membrane)
key_terms.يَدْبُغُ: It tans/hardens/strengthens (metaphor for strengthening the stomach lining)

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of eating pomegranate with its lining according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the medicinal benefits of consuming pomegranates with their inner lining (shahm), noting it strengthens the stomach and enhances intellectual capacity. This recommendation aligns with the Shia tradition of *al-tibb al-nabawi* (Prophetic medicine), where natural remedies are viewed as divine signs for physical and spiritual well-being. The emphasis on 'increasing in intellect' (al-dhihn) reflects the holistic Shia view that physical health directly supports cognitive and spiritual clarity.
